purpose: Index of Learning Lab lessons. Metadata separates educational examples from source-verified policy content.

status_legend.illustrative: Invented scenario or example; not an actual Pennsylvania rule or payment rate.
status_legend.source_review_required: Requires source extraction and applicability review before any policy conclusion can be taught as factual.
status_legend.source_verified: May only be used when source version, effective date, section, applicability, and reviewer have been recorded.

lessons.title: Insurance isn't an appointment
objectives: Separate insurance coverage from actual appointment availability.
Name missing facts without inventing a policy answer.

lessons.title: Follow the money
objectives: Distinguish funding transfers, prospective payments, and service claims.
Explain why accounting boundaries matter before combining totals.

lessons.title: A claim is a question, not a payment
objectives: Distinguish paid, not-approved, and needs-review toy outcomes.
Explain why missing information is not proof that care is uncovered.

lessons.title: Insurance words without the jargon
objectives: Explain key terms in plain language.
Recognize that actual meanings depend on governing program and contract documents.

lessons.title: How to read a policy source
objectives: Locate title, publisher, version, effective date, section, applicability, and exact passage.
Identify what evidence is still missing before encoding a rule.

lessons.title: Pennsylvania behavioral-health financing
objectives: Distinguish pages that have been located from detailed payment rules that remain unverified.

lessons.title: Who are the insurance plans in Pennsylvania?
objectives: Distinguish commercial insurance, Medicaid physical HealthChoices, Behavioral HealthChoices, CHIP, and Medicare.
Find the official current directory for each coverage lane.
Explain why a plan's existence does not prove a specific clinician is in network.
